ORG-01.prompt: When starting a larger venture, how likely are you to clarify specific next steps before getting properly underway?

EXP-01.prompt: A situation immediately feels familiar. You cannot yet say exactly why, but you recognize a pattern from the past. How seriously do you take this impression?

VOICE-01.prompt: Your group has already agreed on a decision. You notice another point against it. How likely are you to raise it anyway?

AMB-01.prompt: You receive very different feedback on the same idea and cannot yet tell which feedback matters more. How uncomfortable does this feel?

DEC-01.prompt: You have the key information for a decision, but there is still some uncertainty. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I prefer to leave the decision open a little longer in case something relevant comes up.
alternatives.B: I commit based on what I know now and change the decision later if there is a good reason.

EL-01.prompt: You are choosing between two approaches, both of which you could try on a small scale. How likely are you to test something before deciding?

EVI-01.prompt: You have three options, and one immediately appeals to you most. How likely are you to deliberately look for reasons against your favorite?

EXP-02.prompt: A solution looks convincing on paper. But you remember things from similar situations that make you skeptical. How much does this experience influence your assessment?

ORG-03.prompt: Several important tasks compete for your attention at the same time. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I keep several tasks moving in parallel so that nothing comes to a complete stop.
alternatives.B: I focus on fewer things and accept that others must wait.

AMB-02.prompt: There are several plausible explanations, but you cannot currently establish which one is right. How uncomfortable does this feel?

EL-03.prompt: You try something and get an unexpected result. What are you more likely to do next?

options.A: I first check whether the result happens again.
options.B: I first try to understand what might have caused it.
options.C: I change something and try another version.
options.D: I use the result alongside what I already know to make the next decision.
options.E: I turn it into a new question to investigate next.

VOICE-02.prompt: You learn something uncomfortable that matters to your work together. How likely are you to raise it soon?

EVI-02.prompt: An important decision depends on an assumption you are unsure about. How likely are you to test that specific assumption before deciding?

DEC-02.prompt: Two options remain plausible. You could do more research but do not expect it to change the overall picture. Which approach do you prefer?

alternatives.A: I still look a little more closely before committing.
alternatives.B: I decide based on what I know by now.

EXP-03.prompt: Based on the available information, two options look about equally good. One strongly reminds you of a similar situation you have experienced. How much does this experience influence your decision?

FS-R1.prompt: You already have a view on an important question. How likely are you to deliberately ask someone you expect to see things differently?

AMB-04.prompt: New information does not make things clearer; it opens up even more possible explanations. How uncomfortable does this feel?

ORG-04.prompt: A task takes much longer than expected. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I first try to finish the task as planned before rearranging the rest.
alternatives.B: I adjust my remaining plan to the new situation early.

EL-02.prompt: You have two plausible approaches and the discussion is not moving forward. Both could be tried with little effort. How likely are you to suggest a test?

EXP-04.prompt: You face a problem you have encountered several times in a similar form. How much do you draw on those experiences to assess what might matter this time?

VOICE-03.prompt: A difficult topic was postponed and never revisited. Something important remains unresolved for you. How likely are you to bring it up again yourself?

EL-05.prompt: An initial attempt gives no clear answer. How likely are you to deliberately change something and try again?

DEC-03.prompt: You have discussed the main arguments for two directions. Some smaller questions remain open. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I want to resolve the open points if possible before the decision is final.
alternatives.B: For me, the decision can already stand despite those open points.

AMB-05.prompt: You need to keep working on something even though an important question remains open. How uncomfortable does this feel?

ORG-02.prompt: A task runs over several weeks, and nobody sets interim deadlines for you. How likely are you to set your own points for reviewing progress?

EVI-03.prompt: You have made a decision. The next day, new information clearly points against it. How likely are you to seriously reconsider your decision?

EL-04.prompt: You are unsure how others would respond to an idea, offer, or approach. With manageable effort, you could show or let them try a simple version. How likely are you to do this early?

ORG-05.prompt: Over an extended period, more work comes in than you can realistically handle. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I try to keep as much as possible moving and make smaller scheduling changes.
alternatives.B: At some point, I draw a clear line and decide again what must wait or be dropped.

EXP-05.prompt: A situation resembles something you know, but not in every respect. How much do you still use your experience as a guide?

VOICE-04.prompt: A decision is made that you consider wrong from a professional perspective. How likely are you to say that you see it differently?

AMB-06.prompt: Two people whose judgment you take seriously assess the same situation very differently. At present, you cannot establish who is more likely to be right. How uncomfortable does this feel?

DEC-04.prompt: You need a direction for the next few weeks, but you know you can decide again later. Which approach do you prefer?

alternatives.A: I keep the options open as long as possible.
alternatives.B: I choose a provisional direction and work with it for now.

EVI-05.prompt: Someone on the team sees something differently and raises a point you can understand. How likely are you to reconsider your own assessment?

ORG-06.prompt: Nobody tells you when or in what order things must be done. How much do you structure the work yourself?

EVI-04.prompt: A result that matters to your venture turns out very differently from what you expected. Which best describes how you respond?

options.A: I first acknowledge that things turned out differently and watch whether it happens again.
options.B: I look for an obvious reason that explains the difference.
options.C: I compare a few possible explanations and then decide whether to investigate further.
options.D: I try to find out which explanation best fits the result.
options.E: I deliberately check explanations that contradict my initial assumption.

FS-R2.prompt: You are stuck on a difficult question. Which approach do you prefer?

alternatives.A: I first keep trying to develop a clearer view on my own.
alternatives.B: I bring in another perspective relatively early.

EXP-06.prompt: You need to decide before all the information is available, but you know the subject very well. How much do you also draw on your experience?

VOICE-05.prompt: The group wants to close a topic, but an important point remains open for you. How likely are you to say that you are not ready yet?

AMB-03.prompt: An important development could have several outcomes, but none can currently be predicted reliably. How uncomfortable does this feel?

ORG-07.prompt: You are concentrating on something important when another important request comes in. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I interrupt my work fairly quickly and take care of the new request.
alternatives.B: I first stay with what I am currently working on.

EVI-06.prompt: Two sources you generally consider reliable contradict each other on an important question. How likely are you to look more closely at why they differ?

EL-06.prompt: An initial attempt points against your original idea. How likely are you to use it to frame a new question for the next attempt?

VOICE-06.prompt: You initially agreed to a plan but later realize that your view has changed. How likely are you to bring this up again yourself?

DEC-R1.prompt: There is no time pressure on an important decision, but the key information is available. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: Without time pressure, I prefer to leave the decision open a little longer.
alternatives.B: Once I know enough, I commit even without external time pressure.

AMB-R1.prompt: You are planning the coming weeks, although two important circumstances could still change significantly. How uncomfortable does this feel?

VOICE-R1.prompt: Everyone on the team agrees quickly, but you still see a risk. How likely are you to raise it anyway?

EVI-R1.prompt: The team quickly agrees on a solution. You notice unresolved points. How likely are you to deliberately check what might count against the solution?

ORG-08.prompt: Your plan still basically works, but several smaller things turn out differently than expected. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I only change my plan when the deviations really matter.
alternatives.B: I prefer to adjust my plan even for smaller changes.

EL-R1.prompt: You want to try something new. How likely are you to clarify in advance how you would recognize whether the attempt helps you?

EXP-R1.prompt: You know a subject well and quickly get a sense of what could work. How much does this first impression influence your further assessment?

ORG-R1.prompt: You have promised to finish something by a specific time. How likely are you to check along the way whether you are still on track?

DEC-R2.prompt: Two approaches remain about equally plausible. How likely are you to commit to one anyway, even without new information?

EVI-04r.prompt: An important result for your venture is very different from what you expected. What would you most likely do first?

options.A: I wait to see whether the result repeats. A single outlier can be misleading.
options.B: I work with the most likely explanation so that we can keep moving.
options.C: I look at how the result came about before interpreting it.
options.D: I consider several possible explanations and weigh them against each other.
options.E: I first ask whether my original expectation was sound.

EL-03r.prompt: You try something out, and the result surprises you. What would you most likely do next?

options.A: I try it again in the same way to see whether the result holds.
options.B: I change one specific thing and try again.
options.C: I try a substantially different approach.
options.D: The result is enough for me to make a decision without another test.

EL-06r.prompt: An initial trial goes against your original idea. How likely are you to consider what you would specifically test differently next time?
